# Helper exposure

<!-- GENERATED by `cargo run -p xtask -- lua-helpers`; do not edit. `--check` fails when this file is not what the classifier says. -->

Every native host helper (`native-hooks.json` plus the pending `tools/native-hook-fragments/`, 403 in all) lands in exactly one class: `generated` (plain args and a supported return: the generator can emit the `horizon.*` bridge), `already-lua` (a hand-written Lua helper already stands behind it), `adapter` (a hand-written converter would unblock it: the table names the blocking types), `handle` (an opaque draw/mod handle, needing its own design), or `cannot` (no bridge, with the reason). `docs/api/hook-exposure.md` is the same idea for hook points. This page is `lua-helpers`'s human-readable record; `crates/event-horizon-lua/src/generated_helpers.rs` is its bridge for the spike set.

53 generated (15 enabled), 64 already-lua, 230 adapter, 30 handle, 26 cannot (403 total). 38 generated helpers are **not enabled**: the spike enables its allowlist (remove_effect, set_attribute_base, set_flight, respawn_player, resend_commands, profile_by_uuid, player_view_distance, player_sneaking, player_stat, hide_entity_from, sleep_ignored, mob_stop, mob_navigating, max_stack_size, refresh_player) and classifies the rest as eligible, not enabled yet.

Converting the top 1 (`EntityRef`) would unblock 23 Adapter helpers; the top 3 (`EntityRef, [i32; 3], [f64; 3]`) would unblock 44; the top 5 (`EntityRef, [i32; 3], [f64; 3], Option<(2 elements)>, LevelRef`) would unblock 65; the top 8 would unblock 76; the top 10 would unblock 87; the top 15 would unblock 102; the top 20 would unblock 116; converting all 115 together would unblock 230 (every Adapter helper, as each lists only those types).

What the generator could not express: a `&mut self` helper returning data (a queued action has no way back; it needs the run_command_as callback design); a `Result` return (no error design yet); a callback/closure parameter (needs that same design); an opaque `&mut` draw/mod handle; and every non-plain type above. Native-name types in the adapter list are all small read conversions of the same kinds.

Generator size: this generator plus its model are hand-written; the emitted bridge and its tests are the output. Counted separately in the report.

## Generated, not enabled yet

These all have plain args and a supported return (the generator can emit them) but are not in the spike's allowlist: their Lua cell in `docs/api/hook-points.md` stays empty, and they reach no one yet.

| `apply_screen_blur` | Requests vanilla's menu background blur for this frame, with a per-frame guard so blur is applied at most once per frame. Returns true if blur was newly requested this frame, or false if it was already applied/requested this frame. API @API:screen_transparent_background@. |
| `biome_name` | The name of biome id `biome` (`minecraft:plains`), as a snapshot's `noise_biome` gives it. None for an unknown id. API @API:chunk_snapshot@. |
| `count_packets` | Keep (or stop keeping) every player's play packets for `native_server_packets`, from now on: while on, each packet costs the network thread a lock and a list entry, so turn it on for a session and off after. Off drops what is kept. A switch for the whole server, shared by every mod. API @API:server_packets@. |
| `dismount` | Takes the entity `entity` (a server player or a mob) off what it rides, as `/ride <entity> dismount` does (Bukkit's `Entity.leaveVehicle`): it lands beside the vehicle, and `native_entity_mount` may refuse. In the level in place; inside a player's hook only the acting player and mobs are reached. True when it got off; false when it rode nothing, was not reached, and on a client. API @API:mount@. |
| `eject_passengers` | Takes every rider off the vehicle `vehicle` (a boat, a minecart or a mob), as `native_dismount` does each (Bukkit's `Entity.eject`): the server players and mobs on it. In the level in place; inside a player's hook only the acting player and mobs are reached. True when one got off; false otherwise and on a client. API @API:mount@. |
| `entity_is_mob` | Whether the entity `id` in `dimension` is a living mob: true for a mob that is alive and not removed, false for an item, a player and any other entity. API @API:dev_helpers@. |
| `has_alt_down` | Whether Alt is pressed (live modifier state). |
| `has_control_down` | Whether Control is pressed (live modifier state). |
| `has_shift_down` | Whether Shift is pressed (live modifier state). |
| `key_down` | Whether the key a keybind is bound to is held: any mapping of Key Binds (`key.zoom`, `key.minimap`, a vanilla one), its own choice or its default. False when the mapping is unknown or unbound, and for a mouse button `native_key` does not name. API @API:extras_helpers@. |
| `level_dimension` | The dimension of the level in place. API @API:lua_console_helpers@. |
| `max_players` | The server's player limit (`max-players`, as `/list` shows it), as Bukkit's `Server.getMaxPlayers`. None while the hub is out of reach and on a client. API @API:server_files@. |
| `menu_blur_radius` | The user's configured menu background blur radius (`menuBackgroundBlurriness` in options.txt, usually 0.0 to 10.0; default 5.0). 0.0 means blur is turned off. API @API:screen_transparent_background@. |
| `mob_attack` | Mob `mob` strikes entity `target` of its level with its own attack, as `Mob.doHurtTarget` does: its attack damage, held weapon and enchantments, knockback, the species' extras (a cave spider's poison, a husk's hunger) and its attack sound, through the damage the game deals any mob's hit. `target` is a living mob or a server's player in the same level, by entity id. No reach or sight check and no swing, as in vanilla, where the attack goal checks and swings first. True when the blow was dealt (whether it hurt is the damage hooks' to tell); false for a level not loaded, no such living mob or target, the mob itself, or a player while a guest's packet is handled (the hub is taken out then). API @API:npc_mob_attack@. |
| `mob_cost_sampling` | Time every mob's own tick (its riders inside it) from now on, or no longer, summed by level and mob type for `native_take_mob_costs`: two clock reads and a map update a mob while on, one thread-local read off. Sampled apart from a performance report's, so both can run. For a lighter profile, turn it on in `ServerTickStart` of one tick in N and off after. Call it from a server hook (it belongs to the server thread). API @API:server_tick_timed@. |
| `mob_follow` | Walks mob `mob` towards where entity `target` (a mob, a player or any other entity of the same level) stands now, as `PathNavigation.moveTo(entity, speed)` does (done within a block). A path to where it is now: to follow it, call it again as it moves (vanilla's follow and attack goals ask every few ticks). False as `native_mob_navigate`, or for no such target in that level. API @API:npc_mob_navigation@. |
| `mod_key` | The key the player chose for a mod's key `name`, else `default` (`key.keyboard.z`), as the WebAssembly mods' keys were kept (`key.<mod id>.<name>` in `horizon-mods.txt`). |
| `mod_screen` | The mod whose own screen is open, if one is (Escape, or another screen replacing it, closes it). API 111. |
| `mod_screen_close` | Closes mod `mod_id`'s own screen, if it is open. API 111. |
| `mod_screen_open` | Opens a screen of mod `mod_id`'s own over the world: the screen hooks fire over it as over any other, so the mod draws it in `native_screen_render_post` and takes its clicks, scroll, keys and typing there; the mouse is freed, and Escape closes it. Every mod's own screen has the `NativeScreenView.id` `mod`, so a mod's screen hooks check `native_mod_screen()` is its own before drawing. It doesn't pause a single-player game (as the inventory doesn't). True when it is open: false while another screen is (or another mod's), over the title screen, a book, a sign editor, a dialog or a prompt, while the world loads, and anywhere but the window's own client (the server thread, a dedicated server). A gamepad can close it (B, Start) but not click on it: its clicks don't reach the mouse hooks. API 111. |
| `mount` | Seats the entity `entity` (a server player or a mob) on the vehicle `vehicle` (a boat, a minecart or a mob), as `/ride <entity> mount <vehicle>` does (Bukkit's `Entity.addPassenger`), with its checks: neither rides already, no loop, a free seat, minecarts carry players only, and `native_entity_mount` may refuse. Both in the level in place. Inside a player's hook only the acting player and mobs are reached. True when it rides now; false otherwise and on a client. API @API:mount@. |
| `on` | Whether the player left mod `mod_id` on in Options > Mods. A mod turned off does nothing (check this first in each hook) until the launcher's next build leaves it out. |
| `playing` | Playing, with nothing over the world: keys and zoom apply. API @API:extras_helpers@. |
| `refresh_biome_colors` | Asks `native_biome_colors` again for every biome and, when the colours differ from those in use, rebuilds every loaded section and the far terrain with them (`LevelRenderer.allChanged`, as changing Biome Blend does). Call it when your colours change (a new season, a new day of a slow fade) and once when the player joins, not every frame: a rebuild takes the workers a few seconds. API 107. |
| `refresh_commands` | A mod changed the commands it registers (`native_register_commands`): at the start of the next server tick every mod is asked again, the commands players may run are rebuilt, and every player on the server is sent their tree again, after `native_player_commands_sent`. Nothing happens where no world is open to players, and nothing for a server whose mods never call it. API @API:refresh_commands@. |
| `remove_entity` | Removes entity `id`, one Horizon keeps without simulating, as `/kill` does (it drops nothing and isn't saved). False for no such entity or another dimension. Mobs go with `native_remove_mob`. API 59. Since API @API:remove_projectiles@ it also takes projectiles (arrows, tridents, snowballs, eggs, pearls, fireballs, wind charges, llama spit, shulker bullets, firework rockets) as `/kill` does, and a server player's fishing bobber (`Entity.discard`; the player in place's, or, outside a guest's turn, any of this level's players'). |
| `run_mod_command` | `native_run_command` that reaches the mods' commands too (Bukkit's `Bukkit.dispatchCommand` from the console): a command a mod registered goes to the mods (`native_perform_console_command`), anything else to vanilla's. Whether it ran: a mod took it, or vanilla's ran without failing. No output, as `native_run_command`. API @API:run_mod_command@. |
| `screen_title` | The open menu's title (the block's name, or the one it was given), as plain text. API 20. |
| `set_setting` | Keeps a mod's setting `key`. |
| `setting` | A mod's setting `key` (one file per key in `native_data_dir`). |
| `sneaking` | Whether the player acting now holds sneak (`Player.isShiftKeyDown`, what `UseOnContext.isSecondaryUseActive` reads in a use hook): a wrench that picks a block up rather than turning it, a crank turned backwards. On a server the acting guest's, as their use runs (`as_guest` holds sneak for them); on a client the player's own key. API @API:host_bridge@. |
| `spans` | Record the server tick's spans for `native_server_tick_timed` (or no longer): elsewhere than on a dedicated server, which records them anyway, the hook fires only while they are on. One switch shared with `HORIZON_SPIKES`, performance reports and every mod: spans stay on while anyone wants them. Spans are recorded on every thread (two clock reads a step): turn them on for a profiling session and off after. Only on a server. API @API:server_tick_timed@. |
| `text_allowed` | Whether the server's chat filter (`server.toml` `[chat_filter]`) lets `text` through: true without a filter, None inside a player's hook (where the server is out of reach). API 62. |
| `text_width` | The width of `text` in GUI pixels. API @API:extras_helpers@. |
| `watch_entity_data` | From now on the entity data the server sends each player (`ClientboundSetEntityDataPacket`) reaches `native_entity_data_to`, until the server stops; only that packet is decoded for it. As `native_watch_server_packets`, it cannot be switched off and works from any thread. @API:entity_data_to@. |
| `watch_server_packets` | From now on every play packet the server sends a player reaches `native_server_packet`, decoded, until the server stops; there is no switching it off, so one mod can't silence another's. Until a mod calls this, nothing is decoded or copied. Any thread, any time, a client included (where nothing is sent). @API:server_packet@. |
| `window` | This `Game` is the window's, not a server's. |
| `world_seed` | The world's seed, as `/seed` prints it (`WorldOptions.seed`, Bukkit's `World.getSeed`): every level of the world generates from it, and `native_chunk_generate` gets the same value. None off a server: a client only knows a hash of its server's seed. API @API:world_seed@. |
